# OsaurusSync for macOS and iOS

Swift package wrapping the Osaurus sync core (`OsaurusSyncFFI.xcframework`). Targets macOS 14+
(arm64) and iOS 17+ (device and arm64 simulator).

This README covers package setup and the Apple-specific pieces. For the full API (reading,
writing, subscriptions, streaming, pairing, errors), see the
[client guide](https://github.com/osaurus-ai/osaurus-sync/blob/main/docs/client-guide.md).

## Adding the package

**From a release, as a local package.** Each GitHub release has
`OsaurusSync-swift-local-<version>.zip`: the package with the generated bindings and the
XCFramework inside, so it needs no download at build time. This is the way to use prereleases,
because the main repository is private and SwiftPM can't fetch its release assets.

```sh
gh release download v0.1.0-beta.4 -R osaurus-ai/osaurus-sync -p 'OsaurusSync-swift-local-*.zip'
unzip OsaurusSync-swift-local-0.1.0-beta.4.zip -d Vendor     # creates Vendor/OsaurusSync
```

Add `Vendor/OsaurusSync` in Xcode with **File > Add Package Dependencies > Add Local**, or from
another package:

```swift
.package(path: "Vendor/OsaurusSync")
```

and link the `OsaurusSync` library. The XCFramework is large (static libraries for three
slices), so either keep `Vendor/OsaurusSync` out of the app's git history and fetch it in a
setup script, or track it with Git LFS. To update, replace the folder with the new release's.

**From the distribution repository.** Once a distribution repository is configured (see
[Releasing](https://github.com/osaurus-ai/osaurus-sync/blob/main/docs/development.md#releasing)),
the release workflow pushes each release's package to it, with a `binaryTarget` that downloads
the XCFramework by URL and checksum. The XCFramework URL points at the main repository's
release, so the download only works without credentials once those releases are public. Then
depend on it by version:

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/osaurus-ai/osaurus-sync-swift", from: "0.1.0")
```

The `OsaurusSync-swift-<version>.zip` release asset is that same package.

**From source.** The repository's own `bindings/swift` package expects
`OsaurusSyncFFI.xcframework` next to `Package.swift`:

- **Build it:** run `scripts/build-xcframework.sh` from the repo root. This also regenerates the
  Swift bindings in `Sources/OsaurusSync/Generated`.
- **Download it:** take `OsaurusSyncFFI.xcframework.zip` from the `xcframework` artifact of a CI
  run, unzip it into `bindings/swift`, and run the build script once to generate the bindings
  (or copy them from a machine that has).

Then add `bindings/swift` to the app as a local package (in Xcode, **File > Add Package
Dependencies > Add Local**), and link the `OsaurusSync` library.

## Building and testing

```sh
scripts/build-xcframework.sh                 # release; PROFILE=dev for a faster debug build
cd bindings/swift && swift test              # macOS
xcodebuild test -scheme OsaurusSync -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16'
scripts/test-ios-sim.sh                      # iOS Simulator without xcodebuild (older runtimes only)
```

The XCFramework has three slices: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-apple-ios` and
`aarch64-apple-ios-sim`. There is no Intel slice.

## API shape

The bindings are generated by UniFFI:

- Methods use Swift argument labels: `core.sendMessage(scope:message:)`.
- Records are structs with `var` fields, and enums with data are Swift enums with associated
  values (`case let .messageAdded(message)`).
- Free functions are top-level: `apiVersion()`, `defaultNetworkConfig()`,
  `localNetworkConfig()`, `generateAgentSecret()`.
- `suspend`, `resume`, `close`, `pairWithOffer`, `fetchAttachment` and `resolveAgent` are
  `async`. Everything else is synchronous and local.
- The package adds `SyncCore.open(dataDirectory:deviceName:...)`, closure-based `subscribe`,
  `subscribeConversations` and `setListener`, `OutgoingMessage.text(_:)`, `SyncError.code`
  and `Platform.current`.

## Opening the core

```swift
import OsaurusSync

let core = try SyncCore.open(
    dataDirectory: appSupport.appendingPathComponent("sync"),
    deviceName: UIDevice.current.name,
    keyStore: KeychainKeyStore(accessGroup: "TEAMID.ai.osaurus.shared")
)
core.setListener { event in /* devices, pairing, identity changes */ }
let sub = try core.subscribe(scope: conversationId) { changes in /* message diffs, streams */ }
```

With the default `network`, devices sync only on the same network. Pass
`network: n0PublicNetworkConfig()` for development and beta builds to sync over the internet
through number0's public servers, and ship your own servers through remote configuration (see
[deployment](https://github.com/osaurus-ai/osaurus-sync/blob/main/docs/deployment.md)).

Callbacks arrive on the core's `osaurus-sync-callbacks` thread in commit order; hop to the main
actor before touching UI. Keep `Subscription` objects alive; dropping one cancels it.

Errors are `SyncError` values with a stable `code` (`SyncErrorCode`); map codes, not `detail`
strings, to user-facing copy.

## Key storage

`KeychainKeyStore` stores the device key and user secret as generic passwords with
`kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`. They are never backed up or migrated, so a
restored or new device always gets a fresh device key. A restored data directory keeps its
history, and `recoveryAvailable()` reports that it's waiting for the 24-word phrase. On macOS, signed apps should use the data protection keychain (the default);
unsigned tools pass `useDataProtectionKeychain: false`.

## iOS integration

### Lifecycle

iOS closes the sockets of suspended apps. Wire the core to the app lifecycle:

```swift
let lifecycle = SyncLifecycle(core: core)   // keep a strong reference
lifecycle.start()
```

On entering the background it calls `suspend()` inside a background task: Loro snapshots are
flushed, the SQLite WAL is checkpointed and the endpoint is closed. Messages written while
suspended wait in the outbox. On entering the foreground it calls `resume()`, which reconnects
and catches up. The core does no networking in the background beyond that task; background
refresh and push wakeups are out of scope.

### History

iOS defaults to recent-only history: the last 90 days sync, and older ranges are fetched on
demand when the user scrolls past `MessagePage.atSyncBoundary` (call `requestHistory`). Override
with `history: .full` or per scope with `setHistoryMode`.

### Backfill on battery and metered networks

```swift
let backfill = BackfillPolicyMonitor(core: core)
backfill.start()
```

Background backfill pauses in Low Power Mode and on expensive (cellular, hotspot) or constrained
(Low Data Mode) paths. Live sync, pairing and on-demand history are unaffected. The same monitor
works on macOS for hotspot and Low Data Mode paths.

### Local network discovery (Info.plist)

Devices on the same network find each other with mDNS. On iOS this requires the local network
permission, so add to the app's Info.plist:

```xml
<key>NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription</key>
<string>Osaurus finds your other devices on this network to sync conversations directly.</string>
<key>NSBonjourServices</key>
<array>
    <string>_osaurus-sync._udp</string>
</array>
```

Without these keys, or if the user declines, set `network.mdns = false`; devices still connect
through discovery and relays, if the app configured them. On cellular, connections are usually relayed rather than direct;
that is expected, and `diagnostics()` reports it per peer.

## Logging

```swift
SyncLogging.useOSLog(level: .info)   // before opening the core; subsystem ai.osaurus.sync
```

Attach `core.supportBundle()` (redacted JSON with counters and recent logs) to support requests.
